rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: Hi. I'm Ana Silva. I think I start today.

rendered.speaker: Ben
rendered.text: Hi Ana, welcome. I'm Ben. Nice to meet you.

rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: Nice to meet you too.

rendered.speaker: Ben
rendered.text: Are you new here?

rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: Yes. I start on the payments team.

rendered.speaker: Ben
rendered.text: Oh, cool. I'm in design. I'm here three years already.

rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: Really? I thought you were new.

rendered.speaker: Ben
rendered.text: No. Actually, almost three years.

rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: OK. And who is your manager?

rendered.speaker: Ben
rendered.text: Sarah. She's upstairs now, actually.

rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: Can I meet her today?

rendered.speaker: Ben
rendered.text: Sure. She has a 1:1 at ten, but she is free after lunch.

rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: After lunch is good for me.

rendered.speaker: Ben
rendered.text: OK, come at two. Second floor, the room with the big table.

rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: Thank you very much, Ben.

rendered.speaker: Ben
rendered.text: No problem. See you at two.

rendered.speaker: Luiza
rendered.text: Hi! Is this seat free?

rendered.speaker: Tom
rendered.text: Sorry — I have my things here. But it's OK, I was leaving.

rendered.speaker: Luiza
rendered.text: Thanks. Hi, I'm Luiza. I'm new on the team.

rendered.speaker: Tom
rendered.text: Tom. Nice to meet you. Where are you from?

rendered.speaker: Luiza
rendered.text: I'm from Recife. I came here two years ago.

rendered.speaker: Tom
rendered.text: Really? And what do you do here?

rendered.speaker: Luiza
rendered.text: I'm a data analyst. I work with the CRM — the customer database.

rendered.speaker: Tom
rendered.text: That's interesting. I work in HR, so I'm in the meeting room all the time.

rendered.speaker: Luiza
rendered.text: Do you like it here?

rendered.speaker: Tom
rendered.text: Mostly, yes. The people are very nice. But the coffee is very bad.

rendered.speaker: Luiza
rendered.text: Ha! That is true in every office.

rendered.speaker: Tom
rendered.text: What did you do in Recife?

rendered.speaker: Luiza
rendered.text: I worked in a bank. Data analysis for the credit team.

rendered.speaker: Tom
rendered.text: And here? You like it?

rendered.speaker: Luiza
rendered.text: Yes, the work is more interesting now. But I miss the weather.

rendered.speaker: Tom
rendered.text: I understand. Three years here and I still miss the sun.

rendered.speaker: Rafael
rendered.text: Hi Rafael? Sorry, Rafael is me. OK, anyway. You are new, yes?

rendered.speaker: Bea
rendered.text: Yes! I am new. I start on Monday.

rendered.speaker: Rafael
rendered.text: Nice. And when you start, do you have a schedule?

rendered.speaker: Bea
rendered.text: On Monday I have an orientation. It's from nine to eleven.

rendered.speaker: Rafael
rendered.text: And after that?

rendered.speaker: Bea
rendered.text: After that I have a stand-up with the team. At half past eleven.

rendered.speaker: Rafael
rendered.text: The stand-up. Is that every day?

rendered.speaker: Bea
rendered.text: Every day at eleven thirty. On Thursday the stand-up is at ten.

rendered.speaker: Rafael
rendered.text: OK, so on Thursday you have no stand-up at eleven.

rendered.speaker: Bea
rendered.text: That's right. I have a workshop instead.

rendered.speaker: Rafael
rendered.text: Good. Can we talk on Tuesday? Fifteen minutes?

rendered.speaker: Bea
rendered.text: Sure. Tuesday is good for me. Let's do 14:00.

rendered.speaker: Rafael
rendered.text: Great. See you then.

rendered.speaker: Nina
rendered.text: Hi. Sorry — can you help me? I'm working on the report.

rendered.speaker: Omar
rendered.text: Sure. What is the problem?

rendered.speaker: Nina
rendered.text: I don't understand this sentence. "The deadline is Thursday." What does "is" mean here?

rendered.speaker: Omar
rendered.text: It means "será". The deadline is Thursday. It is in the future.

rendered.speaker: Nina
rendered.text: Ah, OK. And "the report is late" — that means it is in the past, yes?

rendered.speaker: Omar
rendered.text: Yes. Late = after the deadline.

rendered.speaker: Nina
rendered.text: I understand now. Thank you very much.

rendered.speaker: Omar
rendered.text: Is working. I mean — it's working now. I am not sure, sorry.

rendered.speaker: Nina
rendered.text: No problem. You're very kind.

rendered.speaker: Omar
rendered.text: Ask me. I am happy to help. I assist the finance team every week.

rendered.speaker: Nina
rendered.text: Thank you. And if I have a question tomorrow?

rendered.speaker: Omar
rendered.text: Ask me again. I am here until six.

rendered.speaker: Nina
rendered.text: Perfect. One more thing — the word "late". Is it "late" or "lately"?

rendered.speaker: Omar
rendered.text: "Late" is after the deadline. "Lately" is recently. Very different!

rendered.speaker: Nina
rendered.text: Late, lately. OK. Thank you, Omar. This is very clear now.

rendered.speaker: Sarah
rendered.text: Right, let's get started. Thanks for coming, everyone. We have a full agenda today, so I'll keep this to thirty minutes. First item is the release. Priya, can you take us through it?

rendered.speaker: Priya
rendered.text: Sure. The release went out on Friday. No rollback, no hotfix. Latency is down about twelve percent since Tuesday.

rendered.speaker: Ahmed
rendered.text: Twelve percent — is that from the cache change, or from the network work?

rendered.speaker: Priya
rendered.text: Mostly the cache change. The network is the same.

rendered.speaker: Sarah
rendered.text: Good. So that's the first thing. Ahmed, you own the dashboard. Can you have it ready by Thursday?

rendered.speaker: Ahmed
rendered.text: Thursday is tight, but yes. I can have it by Thursday EOD.

rendered.speaker: Sarah
rendered.text: Noted — action item for Ahmed, Thursday EOD. Any questions before we move on?

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: One thing. Are we still shipping the Portuguese version in the same release?

rendered.speaker: Sarah
rendered.text: Yes, same release. OK — that's the first item done. Let's go to number two.

rendered.speaker: Carla
rendered.text: Hi, Marco. Do you have two minutes?

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: Sure. What's up?

rendered.speaker: Carla
rendered.text: I'm building a dashboard for the sales team and I have a question. I'm not familiar with some of these terms.

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: Sure, go ahead.

rendered.speaker: Carla
rendered.text: OK. The report shows churn, right? That's the number we watch every month?

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: Yes. Churn is the percentage of customers who leave. And the KPI next to it is retention.

rendered.speaker: Carla
rendered.text: Retention. OK. And bandwidth — I think I read that somewhere. Is that the traffic?

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: Not exactly. Bandwidth is capacity — how much the system can carry. Traffic is what actually goes through. They're different.

rendered.speaker: Carla
rendered.text: Got it. One more: the stakeholder list has six names. Is that everyone?

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: That's the internal list. The external one has three more, but I'm not sure who owns it.

rendered.speaker: Carla
rendered.text: OK, thanks. That helps a lot.

rendered.speaker: Diego
rendered.text: Hi Elena. Do you have a moment? I wanted to ask about the release date.

rendered.speaker: Elena
rendered.text: Of course. Go ahead.

rendered.speaker: Diego
rendered.text: We're tracking the payments work. The ETA is the fifteenth, but the last two tickets are still open.

rendered.speaker: Elena
rendered.text: I see. So the fifteenth is at risk.

rendered.speaker: Diego
rendered.text: Yes. I think we would need to push it to the end of the month.

rendered.speaker: Elena
rendered.text: Hm. That's a big slip. Can you split it? Ship what you have and circle back on the rest?

rendered.speaker: Diego
rendered.text: That's possible. I could cut the scope to the three things that are actually blocked.

rendered.speaker: Elena
rendered.text: I think that could work. Let me check with the CFO, because there may be a demo on the twentieth. Can you give me an answer by EOD tomorrow?

rendered.speaker: Diego
rendered.text: Sure. I'll have something by EOD tomorrow.

rendered.speaker: Agent
rendered.text: Thanks for calling. What seems to be the problem?

rendered.speaker: User
rendered.text: Hi. I can't log in to the dashboard. I tried three times.

rendered.speaker: Agent
rendered.text: Okay. When did this start?

rendered.speaker: User
rendered.text: It started yesterday afternoon. I think it started after the deploy, but I'm not sure.

rendered.speaker: Agent
rendered.text: Can you reproduce it now?

rendered.speaker: User
rendered.text: Yes. Same thing. The page loads and then the button doesn't work.

rendered.speaker: Agent
rendered.text: Right. Do you have a screenshot?

rendered.speaker: User
rendered.text: I have one. I can send it by email.

rendered.speaker: Agent
rendered.text: Perfect. And which environment — production or staging?

rendered.speaker: User
rendered.text: Production.

rendered.speaker: Agent
rendered.text: Okay. I'm going to log this as a P1 and escalate it to the platform team. You'll get an update by end of day.

rendered.speaker: User
rendered.text: Thanks. That's good to know.

rendered.speaker: Nadia
rendered.text: Hey, Marco. Do you have a minute? I want to touch base on the API work.

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: Sure. What's the situation?

rendered.speaker: Nadia
rendered.text: We finished the first part. The second part is bigger than we thought.

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: How much bigger?

rendered.speaker: Nadia
rendered.text: It's sensible to split it. So I want to propose two phases.

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: That makes sense. What do you need from me?

rendered.speaker: Nadia
rendered.text: I need a decision by Friday. After that the window closes.

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: OK. I'll look at it today and we can circle back tomorrow.

rendered.speaker: Nadia
rendered.text: Perfect. Send me an email and I'll reply.

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: Will do. And do you want me to bring the numbers too?

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: Fine. I'll bring the estimate and the risk list.

rendered.speaker: Nadia
rendered.text: Great. Thank you, Marco. Talk to you tomorrow.

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: Sarah, this is Ana. She joined the payments team today.

rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: Hi, Sarah. Nice to meet you. I'm Ana, from the payments team.

rendered.speaker: Sarah
rendered.text: Welcome, Ana. I'm Sarah, the team lead. I heard about your last project.

rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: Thank you, Sarah.

rendered.speaker: Sarah
rendered.text: Good. Standup is at nine every day, and it's short.

rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: Nine. Who do I work with?

rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: Thanks. Marco, when can we start?

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: Any time before four. I have a build to show you.

rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: Four o'clock. Noted. I have a meeting at ten, then I'm free.

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: Great. I'll send an invite.

rendered.speaker: Sarah
rendered.text: Ana, you're in the Friday review too, right?

rendered.speaker: Ana
rendered.text: Yes, I am. Looking forward to it.

rendered.speaker: Marco
rendered.text: See you both at ten.

rendered.speaker: Lead
rendered.text: Thanks for coming. This is about the outage on Tuesday. I want to be clear about one thing first: this is a blameless review. We're not here to find a person to blame.

rendered.speaker: Dev
rendered.text: Understood.

rendered.speaker: Lead
rendered.text: What we know is this. The service went down at 14:20 and it was back at 15:05. Forty-five minutes. In that window, roughly thirty percent of requests failed.

rendered.speaker: SRE
rendered.text: The likely contributing factor was a configuration change that went out at 14:12. Eight minutes before.

rendered.speaker: Dev
rendered.text: Did the monitoring catch it?

rendered.speaker: SRE
rendered.text: It did not. The alert fired at 14:23 — three minutes after the first failure. I think the threshold was set too high.

rendered.speaker: Lead
rendered.text: I wouldn't say that yet. Let's ask why the threshold was set that way before we decide it was wrong.

rendered.speaker: Dev
rendered.text: Fair. One thing I want to add: I was on call. I didn't escalate faster because I thought the alert was a false positive. That was my call and it cost us about ten minutes.

rendered.speaker: Lead
rendered.text: Thank you for saying that. It's useful. It's not on you alone.

rendered.speaker: SRE
rendered.text: Agreed. My paging policy is the bigger issue.

rendered.speaker: Lead
rendered.text: Right. Two action items. First, page earlier — SRE, can you own that? Second, write this up as a postmortem by Friday. I'll review it.

rendered.speaker: Reviewer
rendered.text: Thanks for coming. Two things on the list. First, the caching layer.

rendered.speaker: Dev
rendered.text: All right.

rendered.speaker: Reviewer
rendered.text: I think we should add a second cache, in front of the API.

rendered.speaker: Dev
rendered.text: Hm. I see the argument, but I'm not sure it's the right trade-off.

rendered.speaker: Reviewer
rendered.text: The hit rate is fifty percent. That's low.

rendered.speaker: Dev
rendered.text: It is. But a second cache adds a failure point. If it goes stale, we serve old data.

rendered.speaker: Reviewer
rendered.text: How often? I mean, how much do we actually save?

rendered.speaker: Dev
rendered.text: Maybe twenty milliseconds. On the checkout path, that's not nothing.

rendered.speaker: Reviewer
rendered.text: I see. So the question is whether twenty milliseconds is worth the complexity.

rendered.speaker: Dev
rendered.text: I think that's the right question. We've had this on the roadmap for three months.

rendered.speaker: Reviewer
rendered.text: Let's keep both options open. Can you write up the trade-off and we decide on Thursday?

rendered.speaker: Dev
rendered.text: Sure. I'll send it tonight.

rendered.speaker: Reviewer
rendered.text: Thanks. And bring the numbers, not just the argument.

rendered.speaker: Dev
rendered.text: Fair enough. I'll bring the numbers. The main site is fine, by the way — it's only the API behind it that is slow.

rendered.speaker: Engineer
rendered.text: What's the difference in practice?

rendered.speaker: Architect
rendered.text: In one, a call to payments is a call. In three, it's a call to payments, then a call to fraud, then a call to ledger.

rendered.speaker: Engineer
rendered.text: So more latency.

rendered.speaker: Architect
rendered.text: Yes. About forty milliseconds per hop, if the services are co-located.

rendered.speaker: Engineer
rendered.text: But we can scale them independently.

rendered.speaker: Architect
rendered.text: That's true. And the failure domain is much smaller. If fraud goes down, checkout still works.

rendered.speaker: Engineer
rendered.text: I see the trade-off now. Latency versus isolation.

rendered.speaker: Architect
rendered.text: Right. And there is a third option — a monolith with a good module boundary.

rendered.speaker: Engineer
rendered.text: That is often the cheapest. And the least exciting.

rendered.speaker: Architect
rendered.text: Exciting is not a requirement. I need to know the numbers.

rendered.speaker: Engineer
rendered.text: I can get the numbers. I need one thing first: what is our target for checkout?

rendered.speaker: Architect
rendered.text: Under eight hundred milliseconds, at the ninety-fifth percentile.

rendered.speaker: Engineer
rendered.text: Then the monolith wins. Three services would put us over.

rendered.speaker: Architect
rendered.text: Let's write that down as a decision. An ADR?

rendered.speaker: Engineer
rendered.text: Yes. And an owner, and a date.

rendered.speaker: Architect
rendered.text: Thursday. Draft it tonight.

rendered.speaker: Engineer
rendered.text: Will do. Right — anything else on the list?

rendered.speaker: Nadia
rendered.text: Yes, please. The two we discussed last week.

rendered.speaker: Sarah
rendered.text: Marco. He's your buddy for the first month. Ask him anything.

rendered.speaker: Architect
rendered.text: Right. Two designs. Option one is a single service. Option two is three.
